residualAnomalyClassification.instruction: Every one of the 7 residual SECTION_NUMBER_SEQUENCE_ANOMALY findings (CONMED 1, DSGR 6) was independently re-inspected against the real underlying document text via scripts/cert-3f1-6-residual-anomaly-inspect.ts - not assumed benign from the finding's own message string.

findingBySite.realPrecedingText: "...accounting terms relating to the Parent Borrower and its Subsidiaries not defined in Section 1.1 and accounting terms partly defined in\n\n" (immediately followed by the spurious match)
findingBySite.mechanism: A genuine in-text citation - 'accounting terms partly defined in Section 1.1, to the extent not defined, shall have the respective meanings given to them under GAAP...' - was accepted as a raw top-level SECTION because the signal phrase actually present ('partly defined in') does not exactly match the gate's regex alternative ('as\\s+defined\\s+in', which requires the literal word 'as' immediately before 'defined'). The gate's own doc-comment lists 'as defined in' as a signal phrase but the regex is stricter than the general concept it names.
findingBySite.verifiedRealMaterialImpact: Confirmed by direct text inspection: the REAL Section 1.2 'Other Definitional Provisions' node's OWN span is truncated at char 158254 (the spurious match's start) instead of extending to char 160021 (where the REAL next section, 1.3 'Exchange Rates', actually begins per the document's own text). Approximately 1,767 characters of genuine Section 1.2 body text (GAAP-related definitional/computational provisions) are misattributed to a spurious sibling node erroneously labeled 'Section 1.1' - which collides in sectionRef identity with the REAL Section 1.1 defined earlier in the same document.

findingBySite.flaggedSectionRef: 2.06 (the REAL heading; the spurious sibling is mislabeled 2.07 and precedes it)
findingBySite.realPrecedingText: "...in the same manner as provided in Section 2.07 with respect to Loans made by such Lender (and Section 2.07 shall apply, mutatis mutandis, to the payment obligations of the Revolving Lenders)..."
findingBySite.mechanism: A genuine in-text citation ('Section 2.07 shall apply, mutatis mutandis, to the payment obligations...') sits inside a parenthetical with NO citation-signal preposition of the gate's own 14-phrase list directly preceding it (the actual preceding text is just the conjunction '(and') - the gate cannot catch a citation that opens a clause as its own grammatical subject rather than following one of the tracked prepositions.
findingBySite.verifiedRealMaterialImpact: The REAL Section 2.05 (Swingline Loans) node's own span is truncated at the spurious 'Section 2.07' match instead of extending to the REAL Section 2.06 (Letters of Credit) heading that genuinely follows it in the document - real Swingline-Lender payment-mechanics prose is misattributed to a spurious duplicate 'Section 2.07' sibling, colliding with the REAL Section 2.07 defined elsewhere in the same document.

findingBySite.flaggedSectionRef: 6.01 (spurious; real heading it corrupts is 6.04's tail / 6.05's head)
findingBySite.realPrecedingText: "...loans and advances by U.S. Loan Parties to Restricted Subsidiaries that are not Loan Parties shall be subject to the terms of\n" (then the spurious 'Section 6.01(b)(iii), determined without regard to...' match)
findingBySite.mechanism: The real phrasing is 'shall be subject to the terms of Section 6.01(b)(iii)' - the gate's 'subject\\s+to' alternative requires the citation-signal words to be the LITERAL last text before the match; the extra words 'the terms of' between 'subject to' and 'Section' defeat the end-anchored regex even though the phrase is unambiguously a citation to the human reader.
findingBySite.verifiedRealMaterialImpact: The REAL Section 6.04 (Investments, Loans, Advances, Guarantees and Acquisitions) node's own span is truncated ~5,729 characters early (from char 457347 instead of extending to the real Section 6.05 at char 463076) - a large block of the actual negative-covenant investment-basket exceptions is misattributed to a spurious duplicate 'Section 6.01' sibling, colliding with the REAL Section 6.01 defined earlier in the document. This same exact mechanism recurs verbatim in DSGR doc-d (a separate real document in the same package) at the equivalent Section 6.01/6.04 boundary.

findingBySite.realPrecedingText: "...another Loan Party or another Restricted Subsidiary in compliance with\n" (then spurious 'Section 6.04), except:' match)
findingBySite.mechanism: Citation-signal phrase actually present is 'in compliance with', which is not one of the gate's 14 tracked phrases at all.
findingBySite.verifiedRealMaterialImpact: Real Section 6.05 (Asset Sales) content is truncated early and misattributed to a spurious duplicate 'Section 6.04' sibling, colliding with the REAL Section 6.04 defined earlier in the document.

findingBySite.flaggedSectionRef: 2.06 (real heading; spurious sibling mislabeled 2.18 precedes it)
findingBySite.realPrecedingText: "...in the case of repayment of another Loan or fees or expenses as provided by\n" (then spurious 'Section 2.18(c), by remittance to the Administrative Agent...' match)
findingBySite.mechanism: Real phrasing is 'as provided by Section 2.18(c)' - the gate's tracked phrase is 'provided\\s+(?:for\\s+)?in' (requires the preposition 'in', never 'by'), so 'provided by' is not caught even though it is semantically identical to the already-tracked 'provided...in'.
findingBySite.verifiedRealMaterialImpact: Same mechanism as the doc-a 2.06/2.07 case above (this is DSGR's Third Amendment restating the identical base-agreement passage) - real Section 2.05 swingline-payment content misattributed to a spurious duplicate 'Section 2.18' sibling, colliding with the REAL Section 2.18 defined elsewhere in the document.

findingBySite.realPrecedingText: "...may be in the form of a notice delivered by the Borrower Representative in accordance with the requirements of\n" (then spurious 'Section 2.03). The deemed payments made...' match)
findingBySite.mechanism: Real phrasing is 'in accordance with the requirements of Section 2.03' - the gate's tracked phrase is 'in\\s+accordance\\s+with' with no allowance for intervening words like 'the requirements of' before the section reference.
findingBySite.verifiedRealMaterialImpact: Real Section 2.09 (Termination and Reduction of Commitments) content is misattributed to a spurious duplicate 'Section 2.03' sibling, colliding with the REAL Section 2.03 defined earlier in the document.

findingBySite.flaggedSectionRef: 6.01 (spurious; same mechanism as doc-a's identical case)
findingBySite.realPrecedingText: "...ity Agreement, and (ii) loans and advances by U.S. Loan Parties to Restricted Subsidiaries that are not Loan Parties shall be subject to the terms of\n"
findingBySite.mechanism: Identical to the doc-a 6.01/6.04 case above (this is DSGR's Second A&R Credit Agreement restating the identical base-agreement passage) - 'subject to the terms of' defeats the 'subject\\s+to' end-anchored regex.
findingBySite.verifiedRealMaterialImpact: Same real investment-covenant-exception misattribution as the doc-a case.

findings.title: P1-10 plausibility gate's citation-signal phrase list is materially narrower than the citation-shaped-in-text-reference concept it is meant to catch, and the exact P1-10 misattachment mechanism (real content truncated from its true parent section and reattributed to a spurious sibling node whose sectionRef collides with a real, distinct node elsewhere in the document) still reproduces in production-relevant real data
findings.evidence: All 7 residual SECTION_NUMBER_SEQUENCE_ANOMALY findings across CONMED (1) and DSGR (6) were independently traced to real source text via scripts/cert-3f1-6-residual-anomaly-inspect.ts. Every single one is a genuine in-text citation ('partly defined in', 'in compliance with', 'as provided by', 'in accordance with the requirements of', 'subject to the terms of', and a bare parenthetical subject with no preceding preposition at all) that the gate's own regex ('under|pursuant to|referred to in|as defined in|set forth in|described in|specified in|contemplated by|required by|permitted by|governed by|in accordance with|subject to|provided (for) in', each end-anchored with no tolerance for intervening words) fails to match because the real phrasing differs from the tracked alternative by one word, an added phrase, or a missing preposition. In every case this reproduces the ORIGINAL P1-10 defect mechanism exactly: the spurious in-text citation is accepted as a raw top-level SECTION, truncating the real enclosing section's OWN span early and re-parenting/misattributing its later real content to a spurious sibling that duplicates a REAL section's sectionRef elsewhere in the same document. This is a citation-identity collision (a real Section 6.01 and a spurious 'Section 6.01' both exist as distinct physical nodeIds sharing the same human-readable label, with the spurious one presenting genuinely different content than the real one under the same label) - directly matching the phase charter's own BLOCKER category 'claim identity conflating siblings' / 'material structural corruption affecting semantics'.
findings.whyThisIsNotDowngradedToInformational: The prior phase's own remediation doc (docs/phase-3f1-5-r-residual-foundation/08-rank-stack-remediation.json, 'residualAnomalies') asserts these are 'non-citation-shaped irregularities (e.g. amendment-restated sections) - consistent with the detection signal's own disclosed heuristic limitation, not evidence the fix is incomplete for the defect it targets.' This certification independently re-inspected the actual document text at every site and found that claim to be FALSE: every one of the 7 sites IS citation-shaped, and the fix IS incomplete for exactly the defect it targets - it was simply never re-tested against phrasing variants beyond the 12-14 phrases enumerated in the original fix's own regression suite. Per the certification charter's own instruction, a BLOCKER is not downgraded because the underlying fix (broadening the phrase list, or replacing exact-phrase matching with a more general 'is this immediately preceded by any non-sentence-terminated prose, regardless of specific wording' signal) looks straightforward.

findings.title: scripts/foundation-audit-known-package-replay.ts's own hardcoded DSGR reconciliation assertion (totalNodes===4149, duplicateLegalLabels===546) was never updated after the P1-10 fix landed and now always prints matchesHistoricalRecord=false
findings.evidence: Independently re-run in this certification; produces totalNodes=4155/duplicateLegalLabels=517 (the correct, current, post-fix numbers matching the prior phase's own remediation doc) but the script's own baked-in comparison still targets the PRE-fix numbers.

verdictReasoning: One BLOCKER (STRUCT-1): the P1-10 fix's own charter requirement - that the exact misattachment mechanism it targets never reproduce in production-relevant real data - is not met. All 7 residual anomalies independently re-classified as MATERIAL_STRUCTURAL_ERROR (0 TRUE_DOCUMENT_IRREGULARITY, 0 BENIGN_PARSER_LIMITATION), directly contradicting the prior phase's own disposition of these findings. Every other structural-integrity invariant tested (identity uniqueness, acyclicity, span containment, hash reproducibility, health-diagnostic accuracy, raw-source-fallback safety) independently passed.
